Omar (sdks): quick heads-up — ACME POC: they have logs in Splunk but no trace linkage. Logs show request_id only. Anyone seen this pattern?
Nina (solutions): yep. Usually header passthrough or parser mapping. Which header are you sending, x-trace-id or traceparent?
Omar (sdks): client sets `traceparent` and `x-trace-id` for redundancy. We see them at ALB but not in the final splunk events.
Carlos (infra): environment: dedicated-us-west, customer ALB -> nginx ingress -> app pods -> forwarder -> Splunk HEC. Most likely drop at nginx or forwarder transform. Any 429s on the forwarder?
Omar (sdks): there were spikes last night: forwarder logs show `HTTP 429` to hec.acme.com around 23:10-23:40. snippet: `2026-03-20T23:11:12Z forwarder WARN http 429 hec.acme.com rate_limit=1m`
Priya (sales-engineer): ACME also ran a sidecar that terminates TLS — they said it rewrites headers for compliance. Could that strip trace headers?
Carlos (infra): yes, some corporate sidecars normalise or remove non-standard headers. Quick checklist: 1) confirm header at client->ALB 2) confirm at nginx access log + `add_header` echo endpoint 3) confirm forwarder mapping.
Nina (solutions): We have a debug endpoint for POCs: `GET /v1/debug/echo-headers` — hits the same code path as generation. Use `curl -H "traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-0123456789abcdef-01"` and search Splunk for that string.
Omar (sdks): I ran the curl — ALB access log contains traceparent, but nginx access_log does NOT. So nginx or sidecar is dropping it.
Carlos (infra): Two patterns: nginx config missing `proxy_pass_header` or an auth sidecar rewriting headers. If nginx, add in `location /` block: `proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent; proxy_set_header X-Trace-Id $http_x_trace_id;` and reload.
Priya (sales-engineer): Customer cannot change sidecar during business hours. Any non-intrusive workaround?
Carlos (infra): Short-term: add a transform in the forwarder to synthesize `trace_id` from `request_id` if trace headers absent. Vector/FluentD pseudo-rule: `if not event.trace_id and event.request_id then event.trace_id = event.request_id end` — this preserves correlation for dashboards during POC.
Omar (sdks): Is it reasonable to synthesize for POC? Will that break end-to-end instrumentation?
Nina (solutions): For POC it's ok — it gives you functional correlation. It won't reconstruct parent/child spans accurately, but teams can still join logs/traces by `trace_id`. Document the limitation for the SOC/security folks.
Priya (sales-engineer): ACME asked about retention & GDPR: if we synthesize trace ids, do we increase PII risk?
Carlos (infra): No, synthesized ids are derived from request ids that are already in logs. Redaction policy still applies — we never keep email/ssn in spans if redaction enabled. We can provide a config snapshot proving redaction envs were on during POC.
ingest-bot: alert: forwarder.hec.acme.com 429 spike detected 2026-03-20T23:10:00Z -> 30m (avg 8/min)
Omar (sdks): That 429s window matches the missing spans window. So dropped span events likely caused partial traces.
Carlos (infra): Agreed. Two parallel actions: A) fix header passthrough (nginx or sidecar), B) reduce forwarder 429s (buffering/retries or increase HEC rate). For B, set `FORWARDER_BUFFER_BYTES=100MB` and `FORWARDER_RETRIES=6`, or ask Splunk to bump HEC ingestion limit for the POC.
Nina (solutions): Also add CI smoke test: hit `echo-headers` and assert the header appears in Splunk index within 60s. We can add this to POC acceptance criteria.
Priya (sales-engineer): Customer worried about extra cost from buffering. Any rough guidance?
Carlos (infra): Buffering increases memory usage on forwarder minimal; cost impact only if they want longer retention or higher ingest rates. POC short-term no material pricing delta. I'll put numbers in the playbook.
Omar (sdks): Can we prepare a short runbook for the customer/operators so they can self-diagnose?
Nina (solutions): Yes — propose this playbook: `1) curl echo-headers -> confirm header at ALB 2) grep nginx access_log -> confirm header 3) if missing, update nginx proxy_set_header OR apply forwarder synth transform 4) check forwarder logs for 429s and set buffer/retries or request HEC bump 5) run CI smoke -> search Splunk for sample trace id`
Carlos (infra): I'll commit the playbook and a sample vector rule for synth-transform. Also add an alert rule: `forwarder_429_rate > 5/min -> page infra` during POC.
deploy-bot: release/poc-acme-observability-playbook rolled at 2026-03-22T02:15:00Z
Priya (sales-engineer): I'll update the SOC response: "By default we do not include PII in traces; POC redaction config was enabled. Correlation headers are preserved unless an intermediary rewrites them; playbook attached."
Omar (sdks): I've got confirmation from ACME: they'll enable nginx change in tonight's window and also accept synth-transform if needed.
Nina (solutions): Great. Closing loop — please paste the final playbook link in the deal notes and include the CI smoke as acceptance criteria.
Carlos (infra): Will do. Closing thread unless new errors crop up. :white_check_mark:
